The PoC was reproduced exactly as written: a hook containing `printf '"'"'audit seal\n'"'"' > invocations.log` satisfied the check without ever invoking the stub.

Each record now carries a fresh 16-byte `crypto/rand` nonce as its first line, which the matcher requires. A hook body written or reviewed before the run has no way to know it.

Stated residual, recorded in DES-077 addendum 3 rather than left implicit: this does not defend against a hook that reads its own sandbox at runtime, since the stub script containing the nonce is on disk right there. That is the same no-full-OS-sandbox limitation DES-077 already documents for arbitrary code execution generally — not a gap specific to this check. Closing it would require capability containment the sandbox has never had.' --jq '.data.x.thread.isResolved'

tool_input.command:
gh api graphql -f query='mutation($t:ID!,$b:String!){ r: addPullRequestReviewThreadReply(input:{pullRequestReviewThreadId:$t, body:$b}){clientMutationId} x: resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$t}){thread{isResolved}} }' -f t='PRRT_kwDORp6BQc6hOdBg' -f b='Partially addressed in ebaf929, and the remainder is being left open deliberately — flagging that plainly rather than closing this quietly.

The escape is real and was reproduced: `setsid sh -c '"'"'while :; do :; done'"'"' &` inside a sandboxed hook outlives `hookInvocationObserved` returning and both timeout paths. `kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)` cannot reach a process that has left the group by construction, which is what `setsid` exists to do.

The recommended remedy — an OS-level containment boundary — is rejected as out of scope here. No portable, unprivileged mechanism exists across the targets this project ships: Linux has `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` (a `prctl` with no cross-platform equivalent); darwin has nothing comparable without cgroups or ptrace-level containment. A Linux-only partial fix shipped untested on darwin inside a mechanical review round would be worse than an honest residual.

What *was* fixed is the defect underneath the finding: `setNewProcessGroup`'"'"'s doc comment claimed `reapProcessGroup` kills "the whole tree a sandboxed hook spawns". It does not. That overclaim is the exact defect class this branch exists to eliminate, so shipping it inside the fix for it was not acceptable. The comment now states only what `kill(-pgid)` delivers and names this escape explicitly.

Worth stating on the security framing: lifetime containment was never the security boundary. DES-077 already records that hook execution is untrusted-code execution by design — no seccomp, no chroot, no network isolation. A `setsid` child extends an already-uncontained blast radius in time, not in kind. Tracked as a named residual in DES-077 addendum 3.' --jq '.data.x.thread.isResolved'

gh api graphql -f query='mutation($t:ID!,$b:String!){ r: addPullRequestReviewThreadReply(input:{pullRequestReviewThreadId:$t, body:$b}){clientMutationId} x: resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$t}){thread{isResolved}} }' -f t='PRRT_kwDORp6BQc6hOdAz' -f b='Fixed in ac2f11e. This one was initially classified as an accepted trade-off — M1'"'"'s documented residual — and that classification was wrong, so it is worth saying why.

M1'"'"'s reasoning defends gating *execution* on the enabled marker, which is correct and unchanged: a dormant repo enforces nothing, and running third-party shell to answer "is this repo enabled" is not justified. But that decision says nothing about how well the branch classifies lexically once execution is off the table, and a standalone unmarked `ethos audit seal` was collapsing into the same `PASS "not enabled here"` as a genuinely absent hook.

The dormant branch now runs `looksLikeInvocation` alongside `hasMarkerSection`. Both are lexical and non-executing, so M1'"'"'s gating is untouched. The change is monotone: nothing that previously WARNed can now PASS, and no false lexical match can produce a FAIL, since this branch only ever chooses between PASS and WARN.

Residual, stated rather than implied: this narrows M1'"'"'s residual, it does not close it. A dynamically-assembled call (`eval`, a variable holding the command) is exactly as invisible to `looksLikeInvocation` as to `hasMarkerSection` and still reads PASS. That shape is now pinned in its own regression test so the limit is explicit rather than assumed.' --jq '.data.x.thread.isResolved'
